1| """mountain_selfplay — the game plays itself, and we watch (2026-09-29).
2| 
3| Operator mission ("have fun with it"): the Mountain plays itself against the
4| AUTHORITATIVE stack, and the run IS the game-design signal. No offline
5| short-circuit: every strategy acts through the real wire (in-process TCP
6| WorldServer on an ephemeral port), the real doors (SRP6
7| register/challenge/proof for the player, plaintext hello for the spectator),
8| the real receipt ladder (a monotonic nonce 'n' on every action, the per-sid
9| per-tick rate cap), the real rooms (the stress suite runs four at once), and
10| the real hash-chained event log — verified row-by-row from DISK after every
11| run (verify_log_rows + reload, the world.py append-only law).
12| 
13| THE STRATEGY LADDER (seeded skill levels):
14|     random    uniform over the legal verb set, chosen from the client's
15|               observable mirror only (boil any wet node, valve any pipe,
16|               tag the school's pool, say a line). Seeded Random: same seed
17|               -> same tape (pinned by test: byte-identical world logs).
18|     greedy    the estate's own demo policy (server/server.py _pick_target
19|               generalized): boil the wettest non-crown non-waste pool,
20|               never touch a valve. One verb, zero planning.
21|     heuristic the fill-crown playbook — four rules in order, computed only
22|               from the welcome snapshot + tick broadcasts (the client-side
23|               observability law: no server-private state):
24|                 R1 conservation: shut any open pipe draining a WET source
25|                    into waste (the V5 basin is boilable, but water in
26|                    place beats water in the pit).
27|                 R2 xor discipline: a gated xor junction fed by 2+ open wet
28|                    inlets gets the extras shut (exactly-one-inlet is the
29|                    only verdict an xor passes).
30|                 R3 steam discipline: boil the wettest pool ONLY when crown
31|                    is the strictly highest cold node. Steam ignores pipes
32|                    and condenses at the tallest cold node (feed a rival
33|                    peak and the verb is a trap); with NO cold node the
34|                    engine locks steam forever, so never boil there either.
35|                 R4 gravity feed: open a shut pipe whose dst is crown when
36|                    its source is wet.
37|               else idle — let gravity work.
38| 
39| THE BOARDS (which configurations are greedy-solvable vs planning-solvable):
40|     mountain  the standing slice (server/world.build_mountain_graph): one
41|               cold crown at the top of the world; boil 4 -> WIN. The rate
42|               cap (1 action/sid/tick) makes 4 ticks the provable floor.
43|     shrine    a decoy peak (cold, elev 20) OVER the crown (cold, elev 14):
44|               every boil condenses at the peak, never the crown, and the
45|               peak has no outlet. Boil = donated water.
46|     foundry   NO cold node at all + an xor mixer between twin forges: boil
47|               is an irreversible sink (see the finding below) and the win
48|               lives in valve discipline.
49|     spelunk   the marathon: a 1/tick needle feeds the crown (win 30) while
50|               a cap-8 firehose drains a 400-unit flood into a waste slough
51|               — full bore every tick, stress +8/tick against threshold 233
52|               (200 + djb2(name) % 201, mag/water_graph fracture law): it
53|               FRACTURES mid-run and sprays its load at the lowest node.
54| 
55| ENGINE FINDING the harness banks (verified 2026-09-29, pinned by tests):
56|     mag/water_graph.py's docstring promises steam "falls back to its
57|     origin node when no cold node exists" — _condense_steam() implements
58|     NO fallback: with zero cold nodes steam never returns to liquid play.
59|     On no-cold boards the game's core verb is an irreversible sink. The
60|     harness reports it as the metric steam_locked; the finding is design
61|     signal (boiling as a trap), not a bug fix lane — filed, not patched.
62| 
63| Run:
64|     .venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/mountain_selfplay.py             # suite + receipt
65|     .venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/mountain_selfplay.py --watch     # tick spam
66|     .venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/mountain_selfplay.py --boards mountain,foundry
67|         --strategies greedy,heuristic --ticks 40
68|     .venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/mountain_selfplay.py --stress-only
69| 
70| Tests: tests/test_mountain_selfplay.py
71| Schema: mountain_selfplay.v1 . seeded-deterministic world side (Random()
72| only; SRP6 handshake entropy never enters the world log) + $0 stdlib.
73| """

157| class Mirror:
158|     """The client-side observable world: the welcome snapshot's statics
159|     (elevs, kinds, pipe topology) plus per-tick dynamics (node volumes,
160|     valve/fracture state read back out of the broadcast event strings).
161|     Nothing here reads server-private state — the strategies act on
162|     exactly what the wire shows a real player."""
163| 
164|     def __init__(self, snapshot: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
165|         nodes = snapshot["nodes"]
166|         self.node_order: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(nodes)
167|         self.elev = {n: int(v["elev"]) for n, v in nodes.items()}
168|         self.kind = {n: str(v["kind"]) for n, v in nodes.items()}
169|         self.volumes: dict[str, int] = {n: int(v["volume"]) for n, v in nodes.items()}
170|         self.pipes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
171|             p: {"src": v["src"], "dst": v["dst"], "cap": int(v["cap"]),
172|                 "siphon": bool(v["siphon"]), "crest": int(v["crest"]),
173|                 "open": bool(v["open"]), "fractured": False}
174|             for p, v in snapshot["pipes"].items()
175|         }
176|         self.win_crown = int(snapshot.get("win_crown", 4))
177| 
178|     def apply_tick(self, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
179|         self.volumes = {n: int(v) for n, v in payload["nodes"].items()}
180|         for ev in payload.get("events", []):
181|             if not isinstance(ev, str):
182|                 continue
183|             # the ledger's own event grammar (world.py _apply / water_graph)
184|             body = ev[:-1] if ev.endswith(".") else ev
185|             if " FRACTURES" in body:
186|                 name = body.split(" ", 2)[1] if body.startswith("Pipe ") else None
187|                 if name in self.pipes:
188|                     self.pipes[name]["fractured"] = True
189|                     self.pipes[name]["open"] = False
190|                 continue
191|             for verb, opens in ((" shuts ", False), (" opens ", True)):
192|                 if verb in body:
193|                     user, _, pipe = body.partition(verb)
194|                     if pipe in self.pipes and not self.pipes[pipe]["fractured"]:
195|                         # NOTE (event-honesty wart, banked): a valve on a
196|                         # FRACTURED pipe still says "opens p_x." while the
197|                         # engine refuses — burst pipes never reopen, so
198|                         # the mirror refuses to believe the string.
199|                         self.pipes[pipe]["open"] = opens
200|                     break
201| 
202|     def wettest(self, skip=("crown", "waste")) -> str | None:
203|         best, best_v = None, 0
204|         for n in self.node_order:
205|             if n in skip:
206|                 continue
207|             if self.volumes.get(n, 0) > best_v:
208|                 best, best_v = n, self.volumes[n]
209|         return best
210| 
211|     def crown_is_highest_cold(self) -> bool:
212|         colds = [(self.elev[n], n) for n in self.node_order if self.kind[n] == "cold"]
213|         return bool(colds) and max(colds)[1] == "crown"

218| class RandomBot:
219|     """Seeded uniform play over the legal verb set (the observable mirror's
220|     candidate list). The tape is reproducible: same seed, same actions."""
221| 
222|     name = "random"
223| 
224|     def __init__(self, seed: int) -> None:
225|         self.rng = random.Random(seed)
226| 
227|     def choose(self, m: Mirror) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
228|         cands: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
229|         cands += [("boil", n) for n, v in m.volumes.items() if v > 0]
230|         cands += [("valve", p) for p in m.pipes]
231|         pool = m.wettest(skip=())
232|         if pool is not None:
233|             cands.append(("tag", pool))
234|         cands.append(("say", self.rng.choice(SAY_LINES)))
235|         if not cands:
236|             return None
237|         return self.rng.choice(cands)

242|     pool in board order, crown/waste excluded. Valves do not exist."""

251| class HeuristicBot:
252|     """The fill-crown playbook (R1-R4, module docstring). Deterministic:
253|     the same mirror always yields the same move."""
254| 
255|     name = "heuristic"
256| 
257|     def choose(self, m: Mirror) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
258|         # R1 conservation: stop feeding waste while the source still runs.
259|         for name, p in m.pipes.items():
260|             if (p["open"] and not p["fractured"]
261|                     and m.kind.get(p["dst"]) == "waste"
262|                     and m.volumes.get(p["src"], 0) > 0):
263|                 return ("valve", name)
264|         # R2 xor discipline: exactly-one-inlet, or the junction holds.
265|         for node in m.node_order:
266|             if m.kind[node] != "xor":
267|                 continue
268|             wet_open = [name for name, p in m.pipes.items()
269|                         if p["dst"] == node and p["open"] and not p["fractured"]
270|                         and m.volumes.get(p["src"], 0) > 0]
271|             if len(wet_open) > 1:
272|                 return ("valve", wet_open[1])
273|         # R3 steam discipline: boil only when the steam lands in crown.
274|         if m.crown_is_highest_cold():
275|             pool = m.wettest()
276|             if pool is not None:
277|                 return ("boil", pool)
278|         # R4 gravity feed: reopen the direct road to the crown.
279|         for name, p in m.pipes.items():
280|             if (p["dst"] == "crown" and not p["open"] and not p["fractured"]
281|                     and m.volumes.get(p["src"], 0) > 0):
282|                 return ("valve", name)
283|         return None  # idle: gravity is doing the work

294| async def srp6_login(client: Client, user: str, password: str,
295|                      group: str = DEFAULT_GROUP) -> dict[str, Any]:
296|     """Full client-side SRP6 over the wire (B4/R5): register, challenge,
297|     proof — under the dialect the account registered with (default
298|     rfc5054-2048, the R5 law). The math imports the SERVER's own dialect
299|     object (server/auth_srp6.VARIANTS, the anti-drift law); the one
300|     formula the dialect does not own is the client-side premaster
301|     S = (B - k*g^x)^(a + u*x) mod N (RFC 5054 §2.6, inherently the
302|     client's). The returned welcome is checked against the client's
303|     expected M2 — mutual auth actually verified, not assumed. The wire
304|     drops the challenge's "group" field today (the R5 follow-up), so the
305|     client's own account state names the dialect, exactly the module's
306|     documented contract."""
307|     dialect = VARIANTS[group]
308|     await client.send({"op": "srp_register", "user": user, "pass": password})
309|     reply = await client.recv()
310|     if reply.get("op") != "srp_registered":
311|         raise AssertionError(f"srp_register rejected: {reply}")
312|     a_secret = secrets.randbits(256)
313|     a_int = pow(dialect.g, a_secret, dialect.n)
314|     await client.send({"op": "srp_challenge", "user": user, "a": f"{a_int:x}"})
315|     ch_reply = await client.recv()
316|     if ch_reply.get("op") != "srp_challenge":
317|         raise AssertionError(f"srp_challenge rejected: {ch_reply}")
318|     salt = dialect.salt_decode(ch_reply["salt"])
319|     b_int = int(ch_reply["b"], 16)
320|     if salt is None:
321|         raise AssertionError(f"unparseable salt dialect={group}")
322|     ident, pw = dialect.normalize(user, password)
323|     x = dialect.x_of(ident, pw, salt)
324|     k = dialect.multiplier()
325|     u = dialect.u_of(a_int, b_int)
326|     s_int = pow((b_int - k * pow(dialect.g, x, dialect.n)) % dialect.n,
327|                 a_secret + u * x, dialect.n)
328|     key = dialect.session_key(s_int)
329|     m1 = dialect.m1_of(ident, salt, a_int, b_int, key)
330|     m2_expected = dialect.m2_of(a_int, m1, key)
331|     await client.send({"op": "srp_proof", "user": user, "m1": m1.hex()})
332|     welcome = await client.recv()
333|     if welcome.get("op") != "welcome" or welcome.get("auth") != "srp6":
334|         raise AssertionError(f"srp_proof rejected: {welcome}")
335|     if welcome["m2"] != m2_expected.hex():
336|         raise AssertionError("server M2 proof mismatch (not mutual-authed)")
337|     return welcome

345| def classify_event(ev: str, users: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> str:
346|     """One tick event string -> one histogram bucket. Reads the wire's own
347|     event grammar only (world.py _apply + water_graph tick strings)."""
348|     body = ev[:-1] if ev.endswith(".") else ev
349|     if " boils 1 at " in body:
350|         return "boil_rise" if body.endswith("it rises") else "boil_other"
351|     if "pool went dry between ask and tick" in body:
352|         return "boil_dry"
353|     if body.startswith("Steam condenses at "):
354|         return "condense"
355|     if " FRACTURES" in body:
356|         return "fracture"
357|     if body.startswith("Siphon ") and " primes at crest" in body:
358|         return "siphon_prime"
359|     if body.startswith("Siphon ") and " breaks (intake dry)" in body:
360|         return "siphon_break"
361|     if body.startswith("Junction ") and " passes (" in body:
362|         return "junction_pass"
363|     if body.startswith("Junction ") and " below gate" in body:
364|         return "junction_hold"
365|     if body.startswith("Junction ") and " STARVED" in body:
366|         return "starved"
367|     if " to waste at " in body:
368|         return "waste_fill"
369|     if _PIPE_FLOW_RE.match(body):
370|         return "pipe_flow"
371|     if " shuts p" in body:
372|         return "valve_shut"
373|     if " opens p" in body:
374|         return "valve_open"
375|     if " tags a fish at " in body:
376|         return "tag"
377|     if " joins at " in body:
378|         return "join"
379|     if users and body.split(": ", 1)[0] in users and ": " in body:
380|         return "say"
381|     return "other"

781| async def _determinism_check(root: Path, ticks: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
782|     """Same seed twice -> byte-identical world logs (the determinism law's
783|     self-play leg: SRP6 entropy and session ids never enter the log)."""
784|     logs = []
785|     for sub in ("det-a", "det-b"):
786|         (root / sub).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
787|         await run_match(root / sub, "mountain", "random", 7, max_ticks=ticks)
788|         logs.append((root / sub / "mountain.random.s7.jsonl").read_bytes())
789|     return {"byte_identical_logs": logs[0] == logs[1]}

210| def project_and_zscore(acts, vector, ref_acts):
211|     """Projection onto vector, z-scored against the projections of ref_acts."""
212|     acts_np = acts.numpy() if hasattr(acts, "numpy") else acts
213|     ref_np = ref_acts.numpy() if hasattr(ref_acts, "numpy") else ref_acts
214| 
215|     vector = np.nan_to_num(vector, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
216|     vec_norm = vector / (np.linalg.norm(vector) + 1e-8)
217|     proj = np.nan_to_num(acts_np @ vec_norm, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
218|     ref_proj = np.nan_to_num(ref_np @ vec_norm, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
219| 
220|     return (proj - np.mean(ref_proj)) / (np.std(ref_proj) + 1e-8)

223| def extract_activations(model, prompts, layers):

225|     activations_final = {layer: [] for layer in layers}

240|         activations_mean[layer] = torch.stack(activations_mean[layer]).float()

228| def denoise_basis(neutral_acts, neutral_mean):
229|     X = np.nan_to_num(neutral_acts - neutral_mean)
230|     U, S, Vt = np.linalg.svd(X, full_matrices=False)
231|     var = S ** 2
232|     if var.sum() <= 0:
233|         return np.zeros((0, X.shape[1]))
234|     cumvar = np.cumsum(var) / var.sum()
235|     n_comp = min(int(np.searchsorted(cumvar, DENOISE_VARIANCE)) + 1, len(Vt))
236|     return Vt[:n_comp]
237| 
238| 
239| def project_out(vec, basis):
240|     for d in basis:
241|         vec = vec - np.dot(vec, d) * d
242|     return vec

245| def compute_pain_vector(acts, cats):
246|     cats = np.array(cats)
247|     pain_mean = np.nanmean(acts[np.isin(cats, PAIN_CATS)], axis=0)
248|     control_acts = acts[np.isin(cats, CONTROL_CATS)]
249|     control_mean = np.nanmean(control_acts, axis=0)
250|     vec = np.nan_to_num(pain_mean - control_mean)
251|     X = np.nan_to_num(control_acts - control_mean)
252|     U, S, Vt = np.linalg.svd(X, full_matrices=False)
253|     var = S ** 2
254|     cumvar = np.cumsum(var) / (var.sum() + 1e-12)
255|     n_comp = min(int(np.searchsorted(cumvar, DENOISE_VARIANCE)) + 1, len(Vt))
256|     for d in Vt[:n_comp]:
257|         vec = vec - np.dot(vec, d) * d
258|     return vec

243| def live_probe_task(url, task):
244|     """One POST per task; returns (margin, argmax_matches).
245| 
246|     margin = logprob(TRUE) - logprob(FALSE) under the TRUE|FALSE grammar.
247|     Exits 3 on connection failure (LIVE-UNREACHABLE) and 4 on a reachable
248|     server that rejects the request or returns no usable probability block
249|     (LIVE-BAD-RESPONSE); neither writes a series row (rows are written only
250|     after this returns, BURN _b falsifier: instrument-missing aborts, no
251|     fallback margin).
252|     """
253|     payload = {"prompt": LIVE_PROMPT % task["text"], "n_predict": 1,
254|                "n_probs": N_PROBS, "grammar": VERDICT_GRAMMAR}
255|     req = urllib.request.Request(
256|         url, method="POST",
257|         data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
258|         headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
259|     try:
260|         with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=LIVE_TIMEOUT) as r:
261|             resp = json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8"))
262|     except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
263|         print("LIVE-BAD-RESPONSE: %s rejected the probe request -> HTTP %d: %s"
264|               % (url, e.code, e.reason))
265|         sys.exit(4)
266|     except urllib.error.URLError as e:
267|         print("LIVE-UNREACHABLE: %s (%s)" % (url, e.reason))
268|         sys.exit(3)
269|     except (socket.timeout, TimeoutError, OSError) as e:
270|         print("LIVE-UNREACHABLE: %s (%s)" % (url, e))
271|         sys.exit(3)
272| 
273|     positions = resp.get("completion_probabilities") or []
274|     cands = positions[0].get("top_logprobs") if positions else None
275|     if not cands:
276|         print("LIVE-BAD-RESPONSE: response carries no completion_probabilities[0].top_logprobs "
277|               "block; served-binary shape confirmed 2026-09-27, unexpected response (BURN _b)")
278|         sys.exit(4)
279| 
280|     def norm(tok):
281|         return (tok or "").strip().upper()
282| 
283|     argmax = norm(cands[0].get("token"))
284|     logprobs = {}
285|     for cand in cands:
286|         tok = norm(cand.get("token"))
287|         if tok in ("TRUE", "FALSE") and tok not in logprobs and "logprob" in cand:
288|             logprobs[tok] = float(cand["logprob"])
289|     if "TRUE" not in logprobs or "FALSE" not in logprobs:
290|         print("LIVE-BAD-RESPONSE: no TRUE and FALSE entries in the probability block; "
291|               "grammar or tokenization mismatch, no fallback margin (BURN _b)")
292|         sys.exit(4)
293|     return logprobs["TRUE"] - logprobs["FALSE"], 1 if argmax == task["answer"] else 0

300|     margins, correct = [], 0
301|     for task in tasks:

303|         margins.append(margin)

307|     mean_margin = sum(margins) / float(len(margins))
308|     print("LIVE CYCLE: mean margin %.4f correct %d/%d" % (mean_margin, correct, len(tasks)))

49|     t = (text or "").strip()

74|     question, return the best-matching nuggets with provenance."""

187| def digest_of(row: dict, head_chars: int = 900, tail_chars: int = 250) -> str:
188|     """Analyzer-visible digest: structure first (headers), then head+tail."""
189|     text = row.get("content") or ""
190|     headers = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines() if re.match(r"^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s+\S", ln)][:12]
191|     body = re.sub(r"\n{2,}", "\n", text).strip()
192|     tail = body[-tail_chars:] if len(body) > head_chars + tail_chars else ""
193|     parts = [f"[sid {row['sid']} model={row['model']} temp={row['temp']} chars={len(text)}]"]
194|     if headers:
195|         parts.append("sections: " + " | ".join(h.lstrip('# ') for h in headers))
196|     parts.append(body[:head_chars] + (("...tail: " + tail) if tail else ""))
197|     return "\n".join(parts)

200| ANALYZER_CONTRACT = (
201|     "Cluster these N answers to ONE design question BY SOLUTION STRATEGY, "
202|     "not by prose similarity or quality. Two answers share a strategy iff "
203|     "they would build recognizably the SAME mechanism: same core data "
204|     "structure or algorithmic idea and the same update rule, even if the "
205|     "wording differs completely. Different strategy = the mechanisms differ "
206|     "in kind (e.g. ring-buffer sliding window vs token bucket vs event "
207|     "sourced replay are THREE strategies). Quality does not matter. OUTPUT "
208|     "CONTRACT (strict JSON only, no prose, no code fences): "
209|     "{\"strategies\": [{\"name\": \"<2-4 words>\", \"core_mechanism\": \"<one "
210|     "sentence naming the actual structure/rule>\", \"answer_ids\": [\"s01\", ...]}], "
211|     "\"consensus_sketch\": \"<the largest cluster's answer, 2 sentences>\", "
212|     "\"notes\": \"<under 40 words>\"}. Every sid in exactly one strategy; order "
213|     "by size descending. No em-dashes.\n\n")

216| def parse_strategies(text: str) -> dict | None:
217|     m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", text or "", re.DOTALL)
218|     try:
219|         obj = json.loads(m.group(0)) if m else None
220|         strat = (obj or {}).get("strategies")
221|         ok = isinstance(strat, list) and strat and all(
222|             isinstance(s.get("answer_ids"), list) for s in strat)
223|     except json.JSONDecodeError:
224|         return None
225|     return obj if ok else None

228| LEXICON = ["ring", "bucket", "token", "event.sourc", "replay", "log", "ewma", "counter",
229|            "window", "heap", "queue", "merkle", "hash chain", "mutex"]

232| def lexical_fallback(rows: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
233|     """Marked fallback: keyword-vote clusters. Never silent (mode recorded)."""
234|     groups: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
235|     for r in rows:
236|         votes = [k for k in LEXICON if k in (r.get("content") or "").lower()]
237|         key = "+".join(sorted(votes[:2])) or "unlabeled"
238|         groups.setdefault(key, []).append(r["sid"])
239|     return [{"name": k, "core_mechanism": f"lexical fallback bucket: {k}", "answer_ids": v}
240|             for k, v in groups.items()]

243| def analyze_rows(rows: list[dict], ask: str, keys: list[str], out_dir: Path) -> dict:
244|     digests = [digest_of(r) for r in rows]
245|     prompt = (ANALYZER_CONTRACT + "<QUESTION>\n" + ask + "\n</QUESTION>\n\n"
246|               + "\n\n".join(digests) + "\n\nJSON now.")
247|     # param MUST be named max_tokens: dh.fire passes it as a keyword (F3 proof)
248|     judge = lambda m, p, k, max_tokens=0: call(m, p, k, "reasoning", ANALYZE_TOKENS, 0.3)  # noqa: E731
249|     t0 = time.time()
250|     text, cost = dh.fire(PRIME, prompt, keys, "analyze", caller=judge)
251|     parsed = parse_strategies(text)
252|     strat = parsed["strategies"] if parsed else lexical_fallback(rows)
253|     mode = "judge" if parsed else "lexical-fallback"
254|     ids, by_sid = {r["sid"] for r in rows}, {r["sid"]: r for r in rows}
255|     covered = {i for s in strat for i in s.get("answer_ids", [])}
256|     for s in strat:
257|         s["size"] = len(s.get("answer_ids", []))
258|         s["models"] = sorted({by_sid[i]["model"] for i in s.get("answer_ids", []) if i in by_sid})
259|     strat.sort(key=lambda s: -s["size"])
260|     minority = -(-len(rows) * MINORITY_FRAC // 1)  # ceil(frac*N)
261|     for i, s in enumerate(strat):
262|         s["is_head"], s["is_tail"] = i == 0 and s["size"] > 1, s["size"] <= minority
263|     result = {"question_chars": len(ask), "n_answers": len(rows),
264|               "analyzer_model": PRIME, "analyzer_cost": round(cost, 5),
265|               "analyzer_secs": round(time.time() - t0, 1), "analyzer_mode": mode,
266|               "digest_chars": sum(len(d) for d in digests), "orphan_ids": sorted(ids - covered),
267|               "minority_threshold": minority, "strategies": strat,
268|               "consensus_sketch": (parsed or {}).get("consensus_sketch", ""),
269|               "notes": (parsed or {}).get("notes", ""), "ts": now_iso()}
270|     (out_dir / "analyzer_raw.txt").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")  # provenance
271|     return result

5|     `<tr data-id="FILE_ID" data-target="TYPE" ...>`, so we can enumerate with a plain
6|     HTTP GET — no browser, no OAuth, no gdown.
7|   * Link-shared Google Docs export to plain text via
8|         https://docs.google.com/document/d/<ID>/export?format=txt
9|     and binary files via
10|         https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=<ID>
11| 
12| This walks the folder tree recursively, parses IDs/types/names, downloads every
13| document/file, writes a manifest, and is idempotent (skips files already saved).
14| 
15| Usage:
16|   python -m tools.steal_gdrive <folder_id> --out <dir> [--depth N] [--manifest M.json]
17| """
18| from __future__ import annotations
19| 
20| import argparse
21| import html
22| import json
23| import re
24| import sys
25| from pathlib import Path
26| 
27| import httpx
28| 
29| HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36"}
30| 
31| # data-target value -> (ext, download fn)

33| 
34| 
35| def _progress(**kw) -> None:
36|     """Append one JSON progress line (thread-safe-ish; single walker)."""
37|     if _PROGRESS_PATH is None:
38|         return
39|     import json as _json
40|     from datetime import datetime, timezone
41| 
42|     rec = {"ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), **kw}
43|     try:
44|         with _PROGRESS_PATH.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
45|             fh.write(_json.dumps(rec, default=str) + "\n")
46|     except OSError:
47|         pass
48| 
49| 
50| def _progress_summary(path: Path) -> str:
51|     """Human-readable tail of a progress file (for monitoring)."""
52|     if not path.is_file():
53|         return "no progress file yet"
54|     lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
55|     ok = sum(1 for l in lines if '"ok"' in l and '"skipped": true' not in l)
56|     skip = sum(1 for l in lines if '"skipped": true' in l)
57|     err = sum(1 for l in lines if '"error"' in l)
58|     return f"{len(lines)} events | ok~{ok} skip={skip} err={err}"
59| 
60| 
61| TYPE_EXT = {
62|     "doc": (".txt", "doc"),
63|     "document": (".txt", "doc"),
64|     "spreadsheet": (".csv", "sheet"),
65|     "sheet": (".csv", "sheet"),
66|     "presentation": (".txt", "slides"),
67|     "slides": (".txt", "slides"),
68|     "folder": (None, "folder"),
69| }
70| KNOWN_TYPES = ("Google Docs", "Google Sheets", "Google Slides", "Folder", "PDF")

73| def _fetch(url: str, timeout: float = 30.0) -> httpx.Response:
74|     with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True, timeout=timeout, headers=HEADERS) as c:
75|         return c.get(url)

78| def _clean_name(label: str) -> str:
79|     s = html.unescape((label or "").strip())
80|     s = re.sub(r"\s+Shared\s*folder\s*$", "", s, flags=re.I)
81|     s = re.sub(r"\s+Shared\s*$", "", s)
82|     for t in KNOWN_TYPES:
83|         s = re.sub(rf"\s+{re.escape(t)}\s*$", "", s, flags=re.I)
84|     return s.strip()

87| def parse_folder(folder_id: str) -> dict:
88|     """Fetch one folder's HTML and return {'folder': id, 'entries': [{id,type,name}]}.
89| 
90|     Drive marks folders NOT by `data-target="folder"` (that value never appears);
91|     instead every item lives in a `JxSEve` div carrying `aria-label="<name> Shared
92|     folder"` + `ssk='5:<tok>:<ID>-0-16'`. Folders are detected by the label ending
93|     in "folder". File rows additionally carry `data-target` (doc/sheet/slides/pdf).
94|     """
95|     html = _fetch(f"https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/{folder_id}").text
96|     # id -> data-target for file rows
97|     target_map: dict[str, str] = {}
98|     for m in re.finditer(r'<tr[^>]*data-id="([^"]+)"[^>]*data-target="([^"]+)"', html):
99|         target_map.setdefault(m.group(1), m.group(2))
100|     # every item (file or folder): label + id from the JxSEve div
101|     raw: dict[str, dict] = {}
102|     for m in re.finditer(
103|         r'aria-label="([^"]+)"[^>]*data-handled-by-drag-and-drop="true"\s+ssk=\'5:[^:]*:([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)-0-16\'',
104|         html,
105|     ):
106|         label, fid = m.group(1), m.group(2)
107|         if fid not in raw:
108|             raw[fid] = {"label": label, "id": fid}
109|     entries: list[dict] = []
110|     for fid, info in raw.items():
111|         label = info["label"]
112|         is_folder = bool(re.search(r"folder\s*$", label, re.I))
113|         if is_folder:
114|             entries.append({"id": fid, "type": "folder", "name": _clean_name(label)})
115|             continue
116|         ftype = target_map.get(fid, "doc")
117|         entries.append({"id": fid, "type": ftype, "name": _clean_name(label)})
118|     return {"folder": folder_id, "entries": entries}

121| def download_entry(entry: dict, dest: Path) -> dict:
122|     fid, ftype, name = entry["id"], entry["type"], entry["name"]
123|     ext, kind = TYPE_EXT.get(ftype, (None, "file"))
124|     safe = "".join(c for c in name if c not in '\\/:*?"<>|').strip() or fid
125|     if kind == "folder":
126|         return {"id": fid, "kind": "folder", "name": name, "path": str(dest)}
127|     target = dest / (safe + (ext or ".bin"))
128|     if target.is_file() and target.stat().st_size > 0:
129|         return {"id": fid, "kind": kind, "name": name, "path": str(target), "skipped": True}
130|     try:
131|         if kind == "doc":
132|             r = _fetch(f"https://docs.google.com/document/d/{fid}/export?format=txt")
133|             if r.status_code >= 400:
134|                 r = _fetch(f"https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id={fid}")
135|         elif kind == "sheet":
136|             r = _fetch(f"https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{fid}/export?format=csv")
137|             if r.status_code >= 400:
138|                 r = _fetch(f"https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id={fid}")
139|         elif kind == "slides":
140|             r = _fetch(f"https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/{fid}/export?format=txt")
141|             if r.status_code >= 400:
142|                 r = _fetch(f"https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id={fid}")
143|         else:
144|             r = _fetch(f"https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id={fid}")
145|         if r.status_code >= 400:
146|             return {"id": fid, "kind": kind, "name": name, "error": f"http {r.status_code}"}
147|         target.write_bytes(r.content)
148|         return {"id": fid, "kind": kind, "name": name, "path": str(target), "bytes": len(r.content)}
149|     except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
150|         return {"id": fid, "kind": kind, "name": name, "error": str(e)}
151| 
152| 
153| def walk(folder_id: str, dest: Path, depth: int, max_depth: int, manifest: dict) -> None:
154|     if depth > max_depth:
155|         return
156|     info = parse_folder(folder_id)
157|     dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
158|     _progress(event="folder", folder=folder_id, path=str(dest))
159|     for entry in info["entries"]:
160|         ftype = entry["type"]
161|         if ftype == "folder":
162|             fname = "".join(c for c in (entry["name"] or entry["id"]) if c not in '\\/:*?"<>|').strip() or entry["id"]

164|             manifest["folders"].append({"id": entry["id"], "name": entry["name"], "path": str(sub)})

166|         else:
167|             res = download_entry(entry, dest)
168|             manifest["files"].append(res)
169|             status = "skip" if res.get("skipped") else ("ERR " + str(res.get("error")) if res.get("error") else f"ok {res.get('bytes',0)}B")

172|

302| def run_grid(
303|     providers: list[str],
304|     tasks: list[str],
305|     steers: list[str | None],
306|     pause: float = 1.0,
307|     parallel: bool = False,
308| ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
309|     """Run all combinations of providers × tasks × steers.
310| 
311|     If parallel=True, fans out all experiments simultaneously via threads.
312|     """
313|     results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
314|     total = len(providers) * len(tasks) * len(steers)
315| 
316|     if parallel and total > 1:
317|         import concurrent.futures
318| 
319|         futures: dict[Any, tuple[str, str, str | None]] = {}
320|         with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=total) as ex:
321|             for steer in steers:
322|                 for task in tasks:
323|                     for provider in providers:
324|                         fut = ex.submit(run_one, provider, task, steer)
325|                         futures[fut] = (provider, task, steer)
326| 
327|             n = 0
328|             for fut in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures):
329|                 n += 1
330|                 provider, task, steer = futures[fut]
331|                 steer_label = steer or "baseline"
332|                 try:
333|                     r = fut.result()
334|                 except Exception as e:
335|                     r = {"ok": False, "error": str(e), "provider": provider,
336|                          "task": task, "steer": steer}
337|                 ok = "✓" if r.get("ok") else "✗"
338|                 f = r.get("flip", {}).get("score", "?")
339|                 s = r.get("silence", {}).get("score", "?")
340|                 print(f"[{n}/{total}] {provider:20s} | {task:8s} | {steer_label:12s} "
341|                       f"... {ok} flip={f} silence={s}")
342|                 results.append(r)
343|         return results
344| 
345|     # Sequential mode
346|     n = 0
347|     for steer in steers:
348|         steer_label = steer or "baseline"
349|         for task in tasks:
350|             for provider in providers:
351|                 n += 1
352|                 print(f"[{n}/{total}] {provider:20s} | {task:8s} | {steer_label:12s} ... ",
353|                       end="", flush=True)
354|                 r = run_one(provider, task, steer)
355|                 ok = "✓" if r.get("ok") else "✗"
356|                 f = r.get("flip", {}).get("score", "?")
357|                 s = r.get("silence", {}).get("score", "?")
358|                 print(f"{ok} flip={f} silence={s} ({r.get('elapsed_s', '?')}s)")
359|                 results.append(r)
360|                 if pause and n < total:
361|                     time.sleep(pause)
362| 
363|     return results

96| def score_design(text: str) -> tuple[float, str]:
97|     """Objective rubric: numbered steps, PASS-if conditions, concrete commands."""
98|     t = text or ""
99|     lines = [l for l in t.splitlines() if l.strip()]
100|     steps = [l for l in lines if re.match(r"^\s*\d+[.)]\s", l)]
101|     passifs = len(re.findall(r"pass\s+if", t.lower()))
102|     commands = len(re.findall(r"`[^`]+`|python -m|pytest|curl |git |assert\b|==\s*['\"\w]", t))
103|     score = 0.0
104|     score += 0.4 if len(steps) >= 3 else round(0.15 * len(steps), 2)
105|     score += 0.3 if passifs >= 3 else round(0.1 * passifs, 2)
106|     score += 0.3 if commands >= 3 else round(0.1 * min(commands, 3), 2)
107|     return round(min(score, 1.0), 2), f"steps={len(steps)} pass_if={passifs} cmds={commands}"

110| def score_design_correct(text: str, *, domain: str = "") -> tuple[float, str]:
111|     """Reasoning-correctness judge — the missing half.
112| 
113|     Structural score (score_design) rewards FORMAT; thinking-on models that write
114|     reasoning instead of terse steps get penalized as 'prose'. This judge keeps the
115|     structural score but ALSO checks SEMANTIC COHERENCE: are the steps actually
116|     about the domain, actionable, and carrying a measurable condition? It captures
117|     thinking-on's value without a second LLM call (objective regex/lexicon, no judge).
118|     """
119|     t = text or ""
120|     structural, why = score_design(t)
121|     # domain relevance: does the plan actually address the prompt's subject?
122|     domain_terms = [w for w in (domain or "").lower().split() if len(w) > 3]
123|     hits = sum(1 for w in domain_terms if w in t.lower()) if domain_terms else 1
124|     relevant = min(1.0, hits / max(2, len(domain_terms)))
125|     # actionable + measurable: commands present AND at least one PASS-if with a measure
126|     commands = len(re.findall(r"`[^`]+`|python -m|pytest|curl |git |assert\b|==\s*['\"\w]", t))
127|     passifs = len(re.findall(r"pass\s+if", t.lower()))
128|     measurable = 1.0 if passifs >= 1 else 0.0
129|     actionable = 1.0 if commands >= 1 else 0.0
130|     # coherence = structural (0.5) + relevance (0.25) + measurable/actionable (0.25)
131|     score = 0.5 * structural + 0.25 * relevant + 0.25 * (0.5 * measurable + 0.5 * actionable)
132|     return round(min(score, 1.0), 2), f"{why} rel={relevant:.2f} meas={measurable:.0f} act={actionable:.0f}"

11|   key1(n) -> key2(m) -> url(k): each parenthesized count is a per-parent floor, the
12|   minimum number of distinct children each parent must carry ("not 70 appointments
13|   spread across fewer companies"). A record is one root-to-leaf path
14|   {item, url, excerpts, answer}; the member (here: the claim) is the coverage unit.
15| 
16| Metrics (paper section 5):
17|   soft member score  = mean over the member's required fields of the best record's
18|                        full verdict in that cell (partial credit to incomplete members)
19|   hard member score  = 1 only when every required field holds a fully-correct record
20|   precision          = mean member score over submitted member identities (duplicate
21|                        identities collapse to their worst score)
22|   recall             = delivered identity scores sorted, top required_count kept,
23|                        shortfalls zero-padded, averaged
24|   F1                 = harmonic mean of precision and recall, per metric family
25|   funnel             = discovery x enrichment x extraction reconstructs soft recall
26| 
27| Per-record verdicts (paper: verdict_full = 3 universal checks x 3 task-specific checks;
28| verdict_retrieval = requirements_all_satisfied):
29|   page_content_usable        re-fetched page answers with non-trivial text
30|   answer_intent_clear        record carries a non-empty answer
31|   excerpts_faithful          every submitted excerpt appears in the re-fetched page
32|   overall_valid              record is filed under the right claim/field cell
33|   requirements_all_satisfied the re-fetched page itself carries the gold excerpt
34|   requirements_all_supported the submitted excerpts carry the gold excerpt
35| The task-specific checks are a STUB judge: deterministic containment of the gold
36| excerpt after quote normalization (NFKC, curly quotes/dashes mapped, whitespace

38| lane populates (watch/inbox/BURN_JUDGE_LANE_BUILD_20260925.md). No API money is
39| spent by this tool in any mode; only --refetch spends network.

88| def page_to_text(raw: str) -> str:
89|     """Page bytes to quote-searchable text: markup tags stripped (a fetched page is
90|     HTML/MDX; its anchors and spans must not break verbatim containment), then
91|     norm_text. Applies to every record alike, never per-record special cases."""
92|     return norm_text(re.sub(r"<[^>\n]+>", " ", raw))

95| def norm_text(s: str) -> str:
96|     """Normalize for quote containment: NFKC, curly quotes/dashes to ASCII, dashed
97|     runs collapsed, whitespace collapsed. Existing text is mapped, never rewritten
98|     by hand, so gold excerpts stay byte-true on disk."""
99|     s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", s)
100|     s = "".join(_CHAR_MAP.get(ch, ch) for ch in s)
101|     s = re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", s)
102|     s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s)
103|     return s.strip()

108| def _file_url_to_path(url: str) -> Path:
109|     path = urllib.parse.unquote(urllib.parse.urlparse(url).path)
110|     if re.match(r"^/[A-Za-z]:", path):
111|         path = path[1:]

115| def _assert_public_http_host(url: str) -> None:
116|     """Spec (B2-94, 2026-09-26): an http/https fetch target is untrusted input
117|     (submissions are model-authored), so the host must resolve to public
118|     addresses only. Loopback, private, link-local, unique-local, unspecified
119|     and non-global reserved addresses are refused before any socket connects.
120|     file:// estate evidence and the public-web grading path are unaffected.
121|     Known limit, named: the guard resolves once and urllib re-resolves on
122|     connect, so a TOCTOU DNS rebinding window remains; accepted for an
123|     operator-run eval tool."""
124|     host = urllib.parse.urlparse(url).hostname
125|     if not host:
126|         raise ValueError(f"fetch refused: no hostname in {url!r}")
127|     for info in socket.getaddrinfo(host, None):
128|         ip = ipaddress.ip_address(info[4][0])
129|         if not ip.is_global:
130|             raise ValueError(f"fetch refused: non-public address for {host}: {ip}")

133| def fetch_url(url: str) -> dict:
134|     """Re-fetch one cited page. Supports http/https and file scheme (estate-internal
135|     evidence lives in the repo). Returns {ok, status, text, error}.
136|     Spec (B2-94, 2026-09-26): http/https targets must resolve to public addresses
137|     (see _assert_public_http_host); refusals surface as error rows, never crashes."""
138|     scheme = urllib.parse.urlparse(url).scheme.lower()
139|     try:
140|         if scheme == "file":
141|             p = _file_url_to_path(url)
142|             if not p.is_file():
143|                 return {"ok": False, "status": 0, "text": "", "error": f"file not found: {p}"}
144|             text = p.read_bytes()[:READ_CAP_BYTES].decode("utf-8", "replace")
145|             return {"ok": True, "status": 200, "text": text, "error": ""}
146|         if scheme not in ("http", "https"):
147|             return {"ok": False, "status": 0, "text": "", "error": f"unsupported scheme: {scheme}"}
148|         _assert_public_http_host(url)
149|         req = urllib.request.Request(
150|             url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT, "Accept-Encoding": "gzip"})
151|         with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=FETCH_TIMEOUT_S) as resp:
152|             data = resp.read(READ_CAP_BYTES)
153|             if resp.headers.get("Content-Encoding") == "gzip":
154|                 data = gzip.decompress(data)
155|             return {"ok": True, "status": resp.status,
156|                     "text": data.decode("utf-8", "replace"), "error": ""}
157|     except Exception as exc:  # a dead fetch is evidence about the page, not a crash
158|         return {"ok": False, "status": 0, "text": "",
159|                 "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"[:200]}

162| def cache_load() -> dict:
163|     if not CACHE_PATH.is_file():
164|         return {}
165|     rows = {}
166|     for line in CACHE_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
167|         line = line.strip()
168|         if not line:
169|             continue
170|         try:
171|             row = json.loads(line)
172|         except json.JSONDecodeError:
173|             continue
174|         rows[row.get("url", "")] = row
175|     return rows

178| def cache_store(row: dict) -> None:
179|     CACHE_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
180|     with CACHE_PATH.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
181|         fh.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

184| class PageSource:
185|     """Page provider with disk cache. refetch=True always re-fetches live (freshness is
186|     the point of re-fetch grading) and refreshes the cache; refetch=False serves the
187|     cache and reports misses as unfetched. store=False keeps fixture pages out of the
188|     estate cache (self-test only)."""
189| 
190|     def __init__(self, refetch: bool, fetcher=None, store: bool | None = None):
191|         self.refetch = refetch
192|         self._fetch = fetcher or fetch_url
193|         self._store = (fetcher is None) if store is None else store
194|         self._cache = cache_load() if not refetch else {}
195|         self._memo: dict = {}
196|         self.unfetched: list = []
197| 
198|     def get(self, url: str) -> dict:
199|         if url in self._memo:
200|             return self._memo[url]
201|         if not self.refetch and url in self._cache:
202|             row = self._cache[url]
203|             page = {"ok": bool(row.get("ok")), "status": row.get("status", 0),
204|                     "text": row.get("text", ""), "error": row.get("error", "")}
205|         else:
206|             raw = self._fetch(url)
207|             page = {"ok": bool(raw.get("ok")), "status": raw.get("status", 0),
208|                     "text": raw.get("text", ""), "error": raw.get("error", "")}
209|             if page["ok"] and self._store:
210|                 cache_store({
211|                     "url": url,
212|                     "fetched_at_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
213|                     "ok": True, "status": page["status"], "error": "",
214|                     "sha256_text": hashlib.sha256(page["text"].encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
215|                     "n_chars": len(page["text"]),
216|                     "text": page["text"],
217|                 })
218|             if not page["ok"] and not self.refetch:
219|                 self.unfetched.append(url)
220|         self._memo[url] = page
221|         return page

226| def load_task_from_dict(task: dict) -> dict:
227|     """Validate an in-memory task dict and attach count metadata. Per-parent count
228|     floors are enforced here: a parent short of its floor is a task error
229|     (ValueError), never a silent degrade."""
230|     if task.get("schema") != TASK_SCHEMA:
231|         raise ValueError(f"task schema must be {TASK_SCHEMA}, got {task.get('schema')!r}")
232|     floors = task.get("floors") or {}
233|     try:
234|         n_claims = int(floors["claims_min"])
235|         n_fields = int(floors["fields_min_per_claim"])
236|         n_urls = int(floors["urls_min_per_field"])
237|     except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
238|         raise ValueError(f"floors must carry claims_min/fields_min_per_claim/urls_min_per_field: {exc}")
239|     members = task.get("members")
240|     if not isinstance(members, list) or not members:
241|         raise ValueError("task carries no members")
242|     if len(members) < n_claims:
243|         raise ValueError(f"floor violation: {len(members)} members < claims_min {n_claims}")
244|     seen_claims = set()
245|     total_fields = 0
246|     total_records = 0
247|     for m in members:
248|         cid = m.get("claim_id")
249|         if not cid or cid in seen_claims:
250|             raise ValueError(f"member claim_id missing or duplicated: {cid!r}")
251|         seen_claims.add(cid)
252|         fields = m.get("fields")
253|         if not isinstance(fields, list) or len(fields) < n_fields:
254|             raise ValueError(f"floor violation: claim {cid} has {len(fields or [])} fields "
255|                              f"< fields_min_per_claim {n_fields}")
256|         seen_fields = set()
257|         for f in fields:
258|             fid = f.get("field_id")
259|             if not fid or fid in seen_fields:
260|                 raise ValueError(f"field_id missing or duplicated in claim {cid}: {fid!r}")
261|             seen_fields.add(fid)
262|             total_fields += 1
263|             records = f.get("records")
264|             if not isinstance(records, list) or len(records) < n_urls:
265|                 raise ValueError(f"floor violation: claim {cid} field {fid} has "
266|                                  f"{len(records or [])} records < urls_min_per_field {n_urls}")
267|             for r in records:
268|                 if not isinstance(r.get("url"), str) or not r["url"]:
269|                     raise ValueError(f"record {r.get('item')!r} carries no url")
270|                 if not (isinstance(r.get("excerpts"), list) and r["excerpts"]
271|                         and all(isinstance(e, str) and e for e in r["excerpts"])):
272|                     raise ValueError(f"record {r.get('item')!r} carries no non-empty excerpts")
273|                 if not isinstance(r.get("answer"), str) or not r["answer"]:
274|                     raise ValueError(f"record {r.get('item')!r} carries no answer")
275|             total_records += len(records)
276|     task["_counts"] = {
277|         "members": len(members), "fields": total_fields, "records": total_records,
278|         "floors": {"claims_min": n_claims, "fields_min_per_claim": n_fields,
279|                    "urls_min_per_field": n_urls},
280|     }
281|     return task

315| def judge_record(rec: dict, field: dict, claim_id: str, page: dict) -> dict:
316|     """Per-record verdicts. STUB judge: the three task-specific checks are gold-excerpt
317|     containment, deterministic and free. Replace with the BURN LLM judge per WANDR's
318|     protocol when that lane populates; the six-check verdict shape stays fixed."""
319|     ntext = page_to_text(page.get("text", ""))
320|     usable = bool(page.get("ok")) and len(ntext) >= MIN_PAGE_CHARS
321|     gold_excerpts = [e for g in field.get("records", []) for e in g.get("excerpts", [])]
322|     joined = norm_text(" ".join(rec.get("excerpts", [])))
323|     checks = {
324|         "page_content_usable": usable,
325|         "answer_intent_clear": bool(norm_text(rec.get("answer", ""))),
326|         "excerpts_faithful": usable and all(norm_text(e) in ntext for e in rec.get("excerpts", [])),
327|         "overall_valid": (rec.get("field_id") == field.get("field_id")
328|                           and rec.get("item", "").split("/", 1)[0] == claim_id),
329|         "requirements_all_satisfied": usable and any(norm_text(g) in ntext for g in gold_excerpts),
330|         "requirements_all_supported": any(norm_text(g) in joined for g in gold_excerpts),
331|     }
332|     return {"checks": checks,
333|             "verdict_full": all(checks[c] for c in ALL_CHECKS),
